events.region: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The island of Hawaii in Hawaii County

* Until 700 PM HST.

* At 349 PM HST, Doppler radar indicated moderate to heavy rain bands
from Hurricane Lala continuing to move onshore across windward and
southeast Big Island. Additional heavy rain bands are anticipated
over the next few hours, especially across the Kau and Puna
Districts. Radar and automated rain gauges are indicating rainfall
rates of 1 to 2.5 inches per hour. Elevated flow was still observed
in Honolii Stream, Wailuku River, and Paauau Gulch. County
emergency management officials have reported numerous road closures
due to flooding in the South Hilo, Puna, and Kau Districts. Flash
flooding is ongoing within the warned area.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hilo, Hawaiian Paradise Park, Kapaau, Honokaa, Volcano, Glenwood,
Mountain View, Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Wood Valley,
Hawaiian Acres Keaau, and Pahala.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek in central
Adams and southwestern Morgan Counties.

* WHEN...Until 900 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying along Bijou creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 739 PM MDT, Local law enforcement reported flooding had
occurred along Bijou Creek through Adams County. Water had caused
closer of a couple county roads, but they have since reopened.
Water had also crested and spilled onto Colfax Avenue in rural
Adams County. The crest has passed this area, but will continue
moving downstream and affect areas farther north through the Hoyt
area and toward the confluence with the South Platte River in
Morgan County.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Bijou Creek.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek.
